issues.location: fourth clause of the complete-branch definition
issues.finding: The used-prefix modal rule is required for every prefix on a branch, but only used successor prefixes of the premise prefix are relevant.
issues.proposed_resolution: Specify every relevant already-used successor prefix in the translated definition.

issues.finding: The true conjunction is missing its prefix; the true disjunction example incorrectly offers false B; and both conditional modal examples omit operands and repeat modal formulas where the rules require signed B at successors.
issues.proposed_resolution: Supply the conjunction prefix, true B in the disjunction branch, complete modal premises and signed B conclusions at the appropriate successor prefixes.

issues.finding: The proof processes only open branches but the proposition demands completeness of every branch, and the proof ends by claiming every branch is closed, contradicting its goal. It also needs a termination reason for repeated modal rule obligations.
issues.proposed_resolution: State that every open branch is complete; explain finite termination by descending modal depth, finitely many subformulas, and one discharge of each fresh-prefix obligation per prefix.

issues.finding: The theorem is stated for arbitrary Gamma, while the proposition used in its proof covers finite Gamma only; the proof also contains a duplicated-verb typo.
issues.proposed_resolution: Run the branch construction for finite Gamma, repair the typo, then apply modal compactness from first-order compactness and the standard translation to arbitrary Gamma.

issues.location: negative conjunction, disjunction and implication induction cases
issues.finding: Three second-conjunct satisfaction conclusions repeat B although their matching signed premises contain C.
issues.proposed_resolution: Use C in each second-conjunct satisfaction conclusion.
